transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-02
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Daniel Cho (Redwood SE), Tom Reynolds (CTO, Ridgeview), Priya Singh (SRE), Liam O'Connor (VP Product)

Summary: Quick walkthrough of Redwood rate-limits and org/project key model; focus on multi-tenant quotas, per-project keys, enforcement modes, and console UX for monitoring. Customer asked about integration with their AWS-hosted services, SSO and audit logging.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya from Redwood, AE on this account. With me is Daniel, our SE who will demo the console and the API pieces. Tom, Priya, Liam — thanks for your time. Sound good?
[00:12] Tom: Yep, thanks. Quick note: we're evaluating how to do per-tenant quotas and a clean keying model for our new virtual-clinic product.
[00:20] Daniel: Great. I'll jump into a live demo. We'll show org keys, project keys, per-key rate limits and also how that surfaces in the Console and via the API. There might be slight lag while I load the demo environment.
[00:35] Priya: One ask up-front — we need the ability to set token-level quotas and also rate per-second caps. We have burst traffic from chat sessions, want predictable throttling.
[00:50] Daniel: Yes we support both token quotas and RPS-style rate limits; you can combine them. We'll show policies that allow burst tokens up to X for short windows then backoff.
[01:05] Liam: Also curious about project separation — how do we map our internal teams/orgs to Redwood org/project keys?
[01:12] Maya: Good q; Redwood supports an umbrella org key for billing and admin, and then project keys for each internal team or product. Project keys can have independent quotas, routing policies, and RBAC scope.
[01:25] Daniel: I'll show the console — here on the left is the org level overview — you can create a project, assign a project key. When you create a key you get an API token scoped to that project and it's visible in the key management page.
[01:42] (screen sharing noise)
[01:55] Daniel: For enforcement we have two modes — soft quotas that emit warnings and hard limits that return 429s. Soft quota is handy for gradual rollouts.
[02:10] Priya: If a key hits limit, do we get a webhook or push alert? We need SRE hooks into PagerDuty.
[02:18] Daniel: Yes you can set alerts in the Console tied to usage thresholds — these can post to webhooks, Slack, or PagerDuty. We also expose metrics to Prometheus via our observability integration for long-term monitoring.
[02:35] Tom: What about per-route limits? We want different limits for text-gen endpoints vs embeddings; embeddings are heavy on tokens.
[02:45] Daniel: You can set per-route and per-model caps. In the policy UI you can scope a rule to model name and endpoint, e.g., /v1/embeddings -> higher token cost weight. We also have token-weight multipliers so embeddings can eat faster through quotas.
[03:05] Liam: Any examples of orgs using this multi-tenant pattern?
[03:12] Maya: Several customers partition by product, create project keys for each tenant class, then apply relative quotas and cost-centers. We can share an anonymized example sheet after.
[03:25] Tom: Security: we need KMS integration for key wrapping and SSO for admin — SAML.
[03:32] Daniel: Redwood supports KMS for customer-managed keys (CMK) and HSM integrations for Private deployments. For hosted we offer envelope encryption with customer KMS in supported clouds, and SAML/SCIM for provisioning RBAC. We'll attach the security pack link.
[03:50] Priya: Cool. Also compliance — SOC 2, ISO?
[03:55] Maya: We are SOC2 Type II and have ISO documentation available; I'll include links.
[04:05] Daniel: Back to rate limits — here's the policy editor. You can define bucket sizes, refill rates, token costs per request. Note the UI also shows simulated impact when you change the values.
[04:25] (typing sounds)
[04:40] Daniel: Now I create a project called virtual-clinic, and I'll provision a project key. The key has metadata fields: owner, environment (prod/stage), and tags for billing.
[05:00] Daniel: I'm going to set a policy: project key default limit 1000 tokens/min, burst up to 3000 tokens for 30s, and a hard 429 after sustained exceed. You can also set daily quotas.
[05:20] Priya: Can daily quotas be shared across multiple projects under same org? For example, global cap across all virtual-clinic projects?
[05:30] Daniel: Yes — policies can be attached at org, project, or key level; org-level quotas can apply across children and you can set precedence rules and inheritance.
[05:45] Tom: How do billing and quotas correlate? We need both cost control and per-tenant SLA gating.
[05:52] Maya: Billing is driven off usage at the org level, but we expose per-project cost breakdowns. You can export usage reports per key daily for chargebacks.
[06:05] Liam: If we do a dedicated deployment later, will the same keys/policies still work?
[06:12] Daniel: Yes — the control plane and key semantics are consistent across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. Policies travel with the org config. In private mode you get additional network restrictions.
[06:25] Priya: Implementation detail — do SDK calls automatically surface the project key or do we need to put it in headers?
[06:33] Daniel: You pass the project key as the Authorization Bearer token. We recommend rotating keys periodically — we support short-lived keys and session tokens for ephemeral workloads.
[06:45] (small cross talk)
[06:50] Tom: What about rate limiting enforcement at the edge vs origin? We're heavy on APIs in front of our services and prefer edge rejects to save compute.
[07:00] Daniel: We have enforcement at the API gateway layer; you can apply limits on the edge proxy to reject before entering the runtime. For hosted customers, we enforce at the edge; for private you can choose where to place enforcement.
[07:18] Priya: Do you support conditional rules, like lower limits during business hours or higher during off-peak?
[07:25] Daniel: Yes, you can schedule policies or use time-window conditions. Also we support dynamic rules via tags and routing policies that can change quota behavior per day-of-week.
[07:40] Liam: Latency concerns — if a request hits a rate limit and we route to fallback model, is there observable tracing?
[07:48] Daniel: We log fallback events, and traces include the routing decision. Console trace view shows per-request latency, which model was chosen, and whether a fallback occurred.
[08:05] Tom: Can we do soft-failover to a smaller model to keep the experience but reduce cost?
[08:12] Daniel: Absolutely — routing policies can downgrade to cheaper model variants automatically when quotas or capacity thresholds hit.
[08:25] (client notes)
[08:40] Priya: About the API: any rate-limit headers returned? We'd like to expose remaining tokens to clients so they can throttle.
[08:48] Daniel: We return standard rate-limit headers (X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, Retry-After) and token-cost headers to help client-side backoff.
[09:02] Maya: We'll also include sample middleware for Node/Python that handles retries and backoff with those headers.
[09:12] Tom: What about concurrency limits for streaming endpoints? We stream a lot for real-time chat.
[09:19] Daniel: You can set concurrent-stream limits per key and per route. There's also a streaming concurrency metric in the console for observability.
[09:35] Liam: Any gotchas with prefix/KV cache interaction and rate limiting? If a lot of cached prefixes reduce tokens, how are quotas metered?
[09:45] Daniel: Good point — we meter based on tokens processed by the runtime. KV cache hits reduce token usage, which reduces quota consumption; cached responses still count toward request count if you have request-based quotas, so you can pick token-based vs request-based depending on what you want to control.
[10:05] Priya: Ok, show us the API example for enforcing a per-tenant daily cap and how an over-limit response looks.
[10:12] Daniel: Sure, here's a curl example. (reads) When the cap is exceeded you'll get a 429 with body mentioning quota type and suggested retry. Headers show remaining token count and reset window.
[10:35] (brief pause, bandwidth blip)
[10:50] Tom: On permissions: can we automate key creation with SCIM so when an internal service is provisioned it gets a project key?
[10:58] Daniel: Yes, SCIM provisioning + our API for key management lets you automate key lifecycle. We also support role tags for minimal privileges.
[11:12] Liam: For the pilot, we'd like three keys: prod-ui, prod-api, staging-api. Can we set different quotas and alerts per key?
[11:20] Daniel: Yep, you can create templates and apply them to multiple keys. We'll provision those during pilot onboarding.
[11:30] Priya: Cost control features — is there an auto-disable if daily spend goes beyond threshold?
[11:38] Daniel: You can set hard spend caps which will disable keys when hit, and soft spend alerts. There's also daily budget automation to throttle down rather than hard stop.
[11:52] Tom: Any logs retention and export policy? We need 1-year audit logs for compliance.
[11:58] Maya: Audit logs are retained per plan; enterprise plans extend retention and allow S3 export. We'll include the retention options.
[12:10] (client side note: "SAML + logging needs to be in doc")
[12:20] Daniel: Quick note: multi-tenant isolation — project keys are cryptographically isolated; you can scope keys to VPC egress in private deployments to prevent cross-tenant data leakage.
[12:35] Liam: How are keys rotated? Do you have an automatic rotation window?
[12:42] Daniel: You can set automated rotation policies; we support zero-downtime rotation with a primary/secondary key swap API.
[12:55] Priya: Demo the console analytics for a single key — how granular are the metrics?
[13:02] Daniel: Metrics are down to 1-minute granularity and include tokens, requests, errors, latency P50/P95, and model-level breakdowns. You can filter by tag or project.
[13:20] (typing)
[13:30] Daniel: Here is a usage chart for prod-api key — you can see spikes, and the alert panel shows a recent throttle event with the exact policy that fired.
[13:50] Tom: Nice, can we export to our internal BI?
[13:55] Maya: Yes CSV export and API for programmatic pulls; we also support direct S3 dump of daily stats.
[14:05] Liam: About multi-region: we need tokens to be processed in EU region for some tenants. How do regional quotas and rate limits interact?
[14:15] Daniel: You can scope keys to regions; policies can be region-aware. If keys are global but you have region routing, quota accounting is global by default, but you can set region-scoped quotas if you need local SLO enforcement.
[14:35] Priya: Any limits on number of project keys per org? We have thousands of microservices.
[14:42] Daniel: No hard limit for most enterprise plans; for very large scale we discuss architecture patterns like service-account pooling to reduce key count.
[14:58] Tom: Back to fallback routing — if model capacity is constrained in a region, can we route to another region's instance while respecting the same quotas?
[15:08] Daniel: Yes, routing policy can fallback to a different region/model and still charge against the same project quota. It's configurable whether routing increases cost or uses lower-cost fallback.
[15:25] Liam: Let's discuss pilot scope and acceptance criteria — we want to run 48-hour spike tests with synthetic chat traffic and measure throttles, fallbacks, and cost.
[15:35] Maya: Sounds good. Proposed accept criteria: less than 1% errors due to throttling under expected load, successful key automation, and visibility in console + S3 export. We'll capture that.
[15:50] Tom: For the spike test, can Redwood provide temporary higher burst allowance?
[15:55] Daniel: Yes during the pilot we can temporarily increase quotas and enable detailed tracing. We'll stage it out so it doesn't affect production.
[16:10] Priya: Any sample policies you can share? It helps our infra team to prototype.
[16:18] Daniel: I'll share a repo with policy templates (curl examples, YAML policy snippets).
[16:28] (screen gesture)
[16:40] Liam: Questions from legal/compliance — do you support data residency options for logs and request content?
[16:48] Maya: Yes, logs and request content can be stored in region-specific buckets for enterprise customers or disabled if required. We'll include options in the security doc.
[17:00] Tom: How long to spin up the pilot environment? We need rapid turnaround.
[17:06] Maya: We can provision trial keys and initial policies within 48 hours; if you want dedicated infra or VPC peering that's a longer lead (2-4 weeks).
[17:18] Priya: Who will be our technical contact?
[17:22] Maya: Daniel will be the SE point for setup and benchmarking. I'll coordinate pricing and procurement.
[17:30] Tom: Great. A few clarifications — can policies be edited via API? We want infra-as-code.
[17:36] Daniel: Yes everything's available via API and SDKs; we also have Terraform provider in beta.
[17:48] (client side: "Terraform provider would be huge")
[17:55] Liam: Last question: do you provide rate-limit grace periods for some keys (VIP customers)?
[18:02] Daniel: Yes, you can mark keys as VIP and apply override policies with higher thresholds and different fallback rules.
[18:18] Maya: Let's recap next steps. We'll send pricing and the security pack; Daniel will send policy templates and example curl/SDK usage. Tom will confirm pilot key names and scope. We'll aim to start pilot next week.
[18:35] Tom: Sounds good. Thanks for the demo.
[18:40] (wrap-up chatter)
[40:00] End call —— note: timestamps after ~18:40 are summary/conclusion and informal chat; total duration ~42 minutes.
